correctness.rationale: The length-two obstruction is exhaustive: a nonsemisimple length-two module has one simple proper submodule, while a semisimple length-two module has only simple proper submodules with pairwise zero intersection, so an isolated vertex always occurs. For nonsemisimple \(\ell\ge3\), \(\operatorname{Soc}(M)\) is a proper universal vertex and always has a distinct adjacent proper submodule, giving a two-set. For mixed semisimple modules, the isotypic decomposition gives explicit adjacent proper submodules whose two open neighborhoods cover every nonzero proper submodule. For homogeneous semisimple modules, the ordinary domination lower bound \(q+1\) is prior; the \(q+1\) hyperplanes through a codimension-two subspace cover the vector space and, because \(\ell\ge3\), share a nonzero common subspace, so the selected hyperplanes also dominate one another. The inspected verifier independently checks representative finite lattices but is not used as the infinite proof.
correctness.risk: The statement uses the graph convention excluding the zero submodule and the whole module.

value.rationale: This is a complete classification of a natural strengthened domination invariant on a standard algebraic graph family. It identifies the exact existence boundary and precisely how the classical ordinary-domination trichotomy changes under the requirement that selected vertices also have selected neighbors.
value.risk: The extension is structurally short once the ordinary classification and socle facts are known, and it is restricted to finite modules.

final_claim: For a finite module \(M\) over a commutative ring with identity, with composition length \(\ell\ge2\), the nonzero-proper-submodule intersection graph has a total dominating set exactly when \(\ell\ge3\). For \(\ell\ge3\), its total domination number is \(|R/\mathfrak m|+1\) when \(M\cong(R/\mathfrak m)^\ell\) is homogeneous semisimple, and is \(2\) otherwise.
limitations: Finite modules over commutative rings with identity only.
Vertices are nonzero proper submodules; conventions including zero behave differently.
